title: 2021 Fall AMC 10B Problem 7
statement: Call a fraction \(\frac{a}{b},\) not necessarily in simplest form, special if \(a\) and \(b\) are positive integers whose sum is \(15.\) How many distinct integers can be written as the sum of two, not necessarily different, special fractions?

solutions.text:
A special fraction with denominator \(b\) equals \(\frac{15-b}{b}=\frac{15}{b}-1,\) where \(1\le b\le14.\) We need integer values of \(\frac{15}{x}+\frac{15}{y}-2.\)

Taking \(x\le y,\) a check of the fourteen possible denominators gives the following pairs that produce integers: \[ \begin{gathered} (1,1),(1,3),(1,5),(2,2),(2,6),\\ (2,10),(3,3),(3,5),(4,12),\\ (5,5),(6,6),(6,10),(10,10). \end{gathered} \] Their distinct sums are \(1,2,3,4,6,7,8,13,16,18,28.\)

There are \(11\) such integers.

Thus, the answer is C .
hints: A special fraction can be written as \(\frac{15}{b}-1\)
